records.gloss: And spoke YHWH to Joshua, saying,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Joshua, saying,

decisions.choice: the LORD spoke to Joshua: the command about the cities of refuge is now carried out
decisions.reason: God had given this command to Moses (Numbers 35:9-15; Deuteronomy 19:1-10). Now that the land west of the Jordan has been divided among the tribes (19:51), God tells Joshua to put it into effect.

records.heading: Cities of refuge

records.source: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר תְּנ֤וּ לָכֶם֙ אֶת־עָרֵ֣י הַמִּקְלָ֔ט אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, saying, give for yourselves the cities of the refuge which I spoke to you by [the] hand of Moses,
pieces: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Appoint the cities of refuge that I told you about through Moses,

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge of which I spoke to you by the hand of Moses,

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Choose the towns of safety that I told you about through Moses.

decisions.choice: cities of refuge: towns where a person who had killed someone could find protection
decisions.reason: The word for refuge means a place where someone is taken in and sheltered. These towns protected a killer from revenge until the case was judged (verses 3, 6; Numbers 35:11-12).

decisions.choice: which I spoke to you through Moses: the laws of Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19
decisions.reason: God refers to what Moses had already taught: six cities, three on each side of the Jordan (Numbers 35:9-34), with the rules for who may flee there (Deuteronomy 19:1-13). Moses had already named the three cities east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 4:41-43).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" names the person through whom something is done or said; Moses was the one who passed God's words on.

decisions.choice: cities of refuge (Literal, Balanced) / towns of safety (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same terms as in Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19. Readable says "towns of safety" so the purpose of the towns is plain.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the words to Israel
decisions.reason: God's words to Joshua open with a double quotation mark; the message Joshua is to give the people opens with a single one here, and both close at the end of verse 6. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma because the sentence runs on into verse 3.

records.source: לָנ֥וּס שָׁ֨מָּה֙ רוֹצֵ֔חַ מַכֵּה־נֶ֥פֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָ֖ה בִּבְלִי־דָ֑עַת וְהָי֤וּ לָכֶם֙ לְמִקְלָ֔ט מִגֹּאֵ֖ל הַדָּֽם׃
records.gloss: to flee there [a] killer, striking [a] person by inadvertence, without knowledge; and they will be for you for refuge from [the] avenger of the blood.
pieces: so that anyone who kills a person by mistake, without meaning to, can flee there. They will be a place of refuge for you from the avenger of blood.

L.3: so that a killer who strikes a person by mistake, without knowing, may flee there; and they shall be for you a refuge from the avenger of blood.

R.3: Anyone who kills a person by accident, without meaning to, can run away to one of these towns. The towns will protect you from the relative who avenges the death.

decisions.choice: killer: anyone who has caused another person's death
decisions.reason: The word names one who has killed someone, whether on purpose or not. In this law it means the one who killed by accident and now needs protection (Numbers 35:11).

decisions.choice: by mistake, without knowledge: without intending it
decisions.reason: The first phrase is the one used in Numbers 35:11, 15 and for unintentional sins (Leviticus 4:2); the second is the one used in Deuteronomy 4:42 and 19:4. Together they stress that the killing was not planned or wanted.

decisions.choice: the avenger of blood: the dead person's close relative, whose duty was to avenge the death
decisions.reason: The word for avenger is the same word as the family redeemer, the relative bound to stand up for the family. Here his duty was to put a murderer to death (Numbers 35:19, 21). The cities protected someone who had killed by accident from him.

decisions.choice: without knowledge: kept, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The oldest Greek translation of Joshua appears to lack this phrase here, as it lacks most of verses 4-6 (see the notes there). This description comes from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against a Greek apparatus by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: anyone who kills a person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the striking was: a blow that killed, as in Numbers 35:11. The words are already inclusive. Readable begins a new sentence and adds "one of these towns" so it is clear where the person runs.

decisions.choice: the relative who avenges the death
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the avenger of blood was, as in Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19.

records.source: וְנָ֞ס אֶל־אַחַ֣ת׀מֵהֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְעָמַד֙ פֶּ֚תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וְדִבֶּ֛ר בְּאָזְנֵ֛י זִקְנֵ֥י־הָעִֽירהַהִ֖יא אֶת־דְּבָרָ֑יו וְאָסְפ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ הָעִ֨ירָה֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנוּ־ל֥וֹ מָק֖וֹם וְיָשַׁ֥ב עִמָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he will flee to one of the cities the these, and he will stand [at the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and he will speak in [the] ears of [the] elders of the city the that his words; and they will gather him into the city to them, and they will give to him [a] place, and he will live with them.
pieces: The one who killed is to flee to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate and explain the case to the elders of that city. Then they are to take {{gender:that person|him}} into the city and give {{gender:them|him}} a place to live among them.

L.4: And he shall flee to one of these cities, and stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and speak his words in the ears of the elders of that city; and they shall take him into the city to themselves and give him a place, and he shall live with them.

R.4: That person must run to one of these towns and stand at the entrance of the town gate. There {{gender:they|he}} must tell the elders of the town what happened. Then the elders must take {{gender:them|him}} into the town and give {{gender:them|him}} a place to live with them.

decisions.choice: verses 4-5: kept, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The oldest Greek translation of Joshua, in its main manuscripts, does not have verses 4 and 5, and its verse 6 is shorter (see verse 6). The added material in the Hebrew uses the wording of Deuteronomy 19:4-6, while the shorter text follows Numbers 35. The Hebrew text is translated here. This description comes from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against a Greek apparatus by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the city gate: the place where the elders heard cases
decisions.reason: In Israel's towns the elders sat at the gate to settle disputes and hear legal cases (Deuteronomy 21:19; 22:15; Ruth 4:1-2). The killer comes there first, before entering the town.

decisions.choice: speak his words in the ears of: tell his case so that they hear it
decisions.reason: To speak "in the ears" of someone is to address them directly. "His words" here are his account of what happened, his side of the case.

decisions.choice: gather him into the city: take him in, give him shelter
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather; used of a person, it means to take someone in as a guest or under protection (Judges 19:15, 18).

decisions.choice: gender setting for the killer
decisions.reason: The law is written with masculine words but covers anyone who killed by accident, as in Numbers 35. Balanced and Readable use the gender setting for the pronouns; Literal keeps the masculine words.

records.source: וְכִ֨י יִרְדֹּ֜ף גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יַסְגִּ֥רוּ אֶת־הָרֹצֵ֖חַ בְּיָד֑וֹ כִּ֤י בִבְלִי־דַ֨עַת֙ הִכָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹֽא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ה֛וּא ל֖וֹ מִתְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃
records.gloss: And if pursues [the] avenger of the blood after him, and not they will deliver the killer into his hand, because without knowledge he struck his neighbor, and not hating he [was] him from yesterday [and the] third day.
pieces: If the avenger of blood comes after {{gender:them|him}}, the elders must not hand the killer over to the avenger, because the killer struck the neighbor without meaning to and had not been that neighbor's enemy before.

L.5: And if the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not hand over the killer into his hand, because he struck his neighbor without knowing, and he was not hating him in time past.

R.5: If the relative who avenges the death chases after {{gender:them|him}}, the elders must not hand the killer over. The killer did not mean to kill the other person and had not hated that person before.

decisions.choice: verse 5: kept, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: As in verse 4: the main manuscripts of the oldest Greek translation lack this verse.

decisions.choice: from yesterday and the third day: before, in time past
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "yesterday and the day before" for any time before. The killer had no past hatred for the one who died, which shows it was not murder (Deuteronomy 4:42; 19:4).

decisions.choice: his neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means a companion or fellow, anyone a person lives and works with, as in Deuteronomy 19:4.

decisions.choice: the elders
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they"; Balanced and Readable name the elders of verse 4 so it is clear who must not hand the killer over.

records.source: וְיָשַׁ֣ב׀בָּעִ֣יר הַהִ֗יא עַד־עָמְד֞וֹ לִפְנֵ֤י הָֽעֵדָה֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט עַד־מוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֑ם אָ֣ז׀יָשׁ֣וּב הָרוֹצֵ֗חַ וּבָ֤א אֶל־עִירוֹ֙ וְאֶל־בֵּית֔וֹ אֶל־הָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־נָ֥ס מִשָּֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And he will live in the city the that until his standing before the congregation for the judgment, until [the] death of the priest the great who will be in the days the those; then will return the killer and will come to his city and to his house, to the city from which he fled.
pieces: The killer is to stay in that city until standing trial before the congregation, and until the death of the high priest who is serving at that time. Then the killer may go back home to {{gender:their|his}} own city and {{gender:their|his}} own house, the city {{gender:they|he}} fled from.'"

L.6: And he shall live in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest who shall be in those days. Then the killer shall return and come to his own city and to his own house, to the city from which he fled.'"

R.6: That person must stay in that town until the community has judged the case. {{gender:They|He}} must stay there until the high priest who is serving at that time dies. After that, the killer may go back home to {{gender:their|his}} own town and house, the town {{gender:they|he}} ran away from.'"

decisions.choice: until ... until: two limits, first the trial, then the high priest's death
decisions.reason: The verse puts two time limits side by side. Numbers 35:12, 24-28 explains how they fit: the killer stays in the city until the congregation hears the case; if the killing is judged an accident, the killer goes back to the city of refuge and stays there until the high priest dies.

decisions.choice: the death of the high priest: the end of the time of refuge
decisions.reason: The killer's protection lasted as long as the high priest then serving was alive; after his death the killer could go home safely (Numbers 35:25, 28). The law does not say why this event ends the time of refuge.

decisions.choice: from "until the death of the high priest" to the end of the verse: kept, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: end the verse at "for judgment", with the Greek
decisions.reason: The main manuscripts of the oldest Greek translation end this verse after "for judgment". As in verse 4, the longer Hebrew text is translated. This description comes from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against a Greek apparatus by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: The message to Israel that began in verse 2 ends here, and so do God's words to Joshua: the single and the double quotation marks close together.

records.source: וַיַּקְדִּ֜שׁוּ אֶת־קֶ֤דֶשׁ בַּגָּלִיל֙ בְּהַ֣ר נַפְתָּלִ֔י וְאֶת־שְׁכֶ֖ם בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־קִרְיַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֛ע הִ֥יא חֶבְר֖וֹן בְּהַ֥ר יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in [the] hill country of Naphtali, and Shechem in [the] hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, in [the] hill country of Judah.
pieces: So they set apart these cities: Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem, in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

L.7: And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

R.7: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart three towns west of the Jordan River: Kedesh in Galilee, in the hills of Naphtali; Shechem, in the hills of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, also called Hebron, in the hills of Judah.

decisions.choice: set apart: dedicate to a sacred purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for making something holy. The towns were set aside by God's command for a special use, as places of protection.

decisions.choice: Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron: one town in the north, one in the center, one in the south
decisions.reason: The three towns lie in the northern, central and southern hill country west of the Jordan, so that each part of the land had a refuge within reach (Deuteronomy 19:3).

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba, that is Hebron: the older name and the later one
decisions.reason: Kiriath-arba was the earlier name of Hebron (14:15; 15:13; Genesis 23:2).

decisions.choice: these cities: (Balanced) / the Israelites ... three towns west of the Jordan River (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced introduces the list with "these cities". Readable also names who set the towns apart and adds that these three were west of the Jordan, to set them beside the three east of it in verse 8.

records.source: וּמֵעֵ֜בֶר לְיַרְדֵּ֤ן יְרִיחוֹ֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה נָתְנ֞וּ אֶת־בֶּ֧צֶר בַּמִּדְבָּ֛ר בַּמִּישֹׁ֖ר מִמַּטֵּ֣ה רְאוּבֵ֑ן וְאֶת־רָאמֹ֤ת בַּגִּלְעָד֙ מִמַּטֵּה־גָ֔ד וְאֶת־גּוֹלָ֥ן בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן מִמַּטֵּ֥ה מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And from [the] other side of [the] Jordan [of] Jericho eastward they gave Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau from [the] tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead from [the] tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from [the] tribe of Manasseh.
pieces: East of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

L.8: And across the Jordan [at] Jericho, eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

R.8: On the east side of the Jordan River, across from Jericho, they chose Bezer in the desert on the high plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: Bezer, Ramoth, Golan: the three eastern cities Moses had named
decisions.reason: Moses had already set these three cities apart east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 4:41-43). Here they are formally given as cities of refuge, from south to north.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan of Jericho: the stretch of the Jordan near Jericho
decisions.reason: "The Jordan of Jericho" names the part of the river opposite Jericho, as in Numbers 22:1. "Across" is said from the land west of the river, and "eastward" makes plain that the east side is meant.

decisions.choice: the plateau: the high tableland north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: The word means level ground. It names the high plain east of the Dead Sea (13:9, 16; Deuteronomy 4:43).

decisions.choice: Golan: the name as read in the margin of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew manuscript writes the name with slightly different letters and notes in the margin how it is to be read. The difference is only one of spelling; both point to Golan (Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 21:27).

decisions.choice: the desert on the high plain
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "wilderness" and "plateau", as in Deuteronomy 4:43.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה הָיוּ֩ עָרֵ֨י הַמּֽוּעָדָ֜ה לְכֹ֣ל׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם לָנ֣וּס שָׁ֔מָּה כָּל־מַכֵּה־נֶ֖פֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָ֑ה וְלֹ֣א יָמ֗וּת בְּיַד֙ גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּ֔ם עַד־עָמְד֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: These were [the] cities of the appointment for all [the] sons of Israel and for the sojourner sojourning among them, to flee there any striking [a] person by inadvertence, and not he will die by [the] hand of [the] avenger of the blood until his standing before the congregation.
pieces: These were the cities designated for all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for the outsiders living among them. Anyone who killed a person by mistake could flee there and not die at the hands of the avenger of blood before standing trial before the congregation.

L.9: These were the appointed cities for all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns among them, for anyone who strikes a person by mistake to flee there, so that he may not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stands before the congregation.

R.9: These were the towns chosen for all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for the outsiders who lived among them. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run away to one of them. Then the relative who avenges the death could not kill {{gender:them|him}} before the community had judged the case.

decisions.choice: cities of the appointment: the designated cities
decisions.reason: The word for appointment is found only here. It comes from a verb meaning to fix or appoint, so the phrase means cities chosen and set for this purpose.

decisions.choice: the sojourner among them: an outsider living in Israel also had the right of refuge
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone from outside Israel who lived among the people without family land. The law of refuge protected such a person just as it protected an Israelite (Numbers 35:15).

decisions.choice: until he stands before the congregation: the protection lasts until the trial
decisions.reason: The city kept the avenger from killing the person before the congregation had heard the case, as in verse 6 and Numbers 35:12.

decisions.choice: sojourner (Literal) / outsiders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The same words as in Leviticus and Numbers for a resident from outside Israel; "foreigner" is kept for another Hebrew word.
